subject: PrivDeploy: role-binding conventions + CI templates for Terraform/Helm/Ansible
messages:
From: Jessica Park <jessica@cloudops.io>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: infra@acme.com
Date: 2026-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private deploy IAC - request: role binding conventions + CI templates

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for agreeing to take a look. Acme's security team ran a quick scan against our initial private-deploy repo and flagged a few policy gaps. Before we hand anything to their procurement/security reviewers, can Redwood review the following and confirm whether your preferred module patterns align with our expectations?

High-level asks:
- Recommended role-binding / RBAC pattern for operator/service accounts that install Helm charts (cluster vs namespace scope).
- Terraform module layout for VPC and cross-host routing (we currently have a single monorepo module).
- CI templates for running plan/apply safely (we have sample GitHub Actions and a Jenkinsfile; want Redwood's suggestions to match your evidence needs).
- Ansible roles that reconcile secrets/credentials post-deploy (we'd like least-privilege patterns).

I've attached: cloudops-priv-iac-scan-results.pdf (scan comments), ci-templates.tar.gz, and a zip of the Ansible roles stub.

Would you and your infra team be able to provide a short checklist or minimal changes we should implement? If it's easier, we can set a 30-minute sync tomorrow.

Thanks,
Jessica
CloudOps Solutions
Attachments: cloudops-priv-iac-scan-results.pdf (pdf), ci-templates.tar.gz (tgz), ansible-roles-stub.zip (zip)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jessica Park <jessica@cloudops.io>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-18T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy IAC - request: role binding conventions + CI templates

Jessica — thanks for the context and the attachments. Quick read-through below; I've included action items and where we'd like evidence links (to include in the audit). If the team prefers, we can convert these into a one-page checklist.

Top-level guidance (short):
- RBAC: prefer namespace-scoped rolebindings for runtime components and cluster-scoped only for controllers that must manage CRDs or nodes. Provide explicit service account names in Helm values.yaml and refuse wildcard bindings.
- Terraform: split networking (VPC, subnets, routing) from platform (k8s cluster, node pools). Each module should expose a small set of outputs used by downstream modules rather than using remote-state for everything.
- CI/CD templates: require a separate plan job that runs against a dry-run workspace plus an approval gate for apply; sign and store the plan artifact in an immutable bucket. Avoid running terraform apply in shared developer contexts.
- Ansible: roles should be idempotent and accept credential references (not raw creds). Use a vault/KMS-backed lookup at runtime and document credential scoping.

Concrete next steps for your team:
1) Share the GitHub repo link for the Terraform modules (we looked at ci-templates.tar.gz but want the repo history).
2) Replace any rolebinding-* wildcard entries in the Helm charts; add example values for serviceAccount.name.
3) Add a CI job that uploads the terraform plan artifact and a short README about approval flow.

Evidence we need for compliance review:
- A sample plan artifact (signed or hashed) and the job that created it (link to action run).
- Helm chart value file demonstrating explicit SA binding.
- Ansible task example showing KMS/vault lookup (no plaintext).

We can do a 30-minute sync 2026-04-19 between 9:00-11:00 PT if that works.

—Karthik
Lead, Private Deployments (Redwood Inference)
Attachments: none
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, Jessica Park <jessica@cloudops.io>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-18T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy IAC - request: role binding conventions + CI templates

Adding a couple of technical checklist items from an evidence/telemetry perspective — hi Jessica, this is the kind of thing our compliance teams will ask for during the next handoff: 

- Telemetry and audits: ensure your CI job emits provenance metadata (commit sha, pipeline id, actor) into the plan artifact metadata. We'll want to link that artifact to the applied state in our acceptance evidence.
- KV cache/secret handling: if the Ansible roles write any secret artifacts to disk, they must be ephemeral and cleaned up post-run; document the cleanup step in the role README.
- Network proof: provide a simple connectivity test job (curl to a control-plane endpoint) that runs post-deploy to verify routable subnets; capture traceroute or route table snapshot as evidence.

Also — Kim, Marissa: can you validate whether our standard Helm operator policies (ns scope only) need any exception here? If Acme requires cluster-scoped CRD management by the operator, we should add a narrowly scoped ClusterRole with only the CRD verbs.

Neha
Security & Compliance (Redwood Inference)
From: Jessica Park <jessica@cloudops.io>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, infra@acme.com
Date: 2026-04-19T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy IAC - request: role binding conventions + CI templates

Thanks — all useful, appreciated. We're going to:
- push a tiny PR that removes the wildcard rolebindings and adds explicit serviceAccount example values (targeting the terraform-helm repo).
- add a plan artifact upload step to our GitHub Actions and attach the provenance fields Neha calls out.
- update the Ansible role README to show the KMS lookup and ephemeral cleanup.

I'll open PRs and ping this thread with links. Tentative sync: 2026-04-20 10:00 PT if that works on your side; otherwise we'll do the 9:00-11:00 PT window you suggested.

-Jessica
CloudOps Solutions
Attachments: none
